test_title: RRB ALP CBT-I 2024 Official Paper (Held On: 28 Nov, 2024 Shift 2)
subject: general
question: The average of 70 values is 40. If each value is multiplied by 20, what will be the changed average?
solution:
__Shortcut Trick__

If each value in a data set is **multiplied** by a constant **k**, the **average** of the set is also multiplied by **k**.

Here, the **Initial Average** is **40** and each value is multiplied by **20**.

**New Average** = **Initial Average** × 20

**New Average** = 40 × 20 = 800.

**∴ The correct answer is 800.**

**__Alternate Method__**

**Given:**

Total number of values (n) = **70**

Average of these values = **40**

**Formula Used:**

Average = (Sum of all values) ÷ (Total number of values)

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/4fd1d9cf3afdfe7a542885642b8144b5d739c9c513e6f4fb0af043d7f674d056.png] 

⇒ Sum of **70 values** = Average × n

⇒ **Initial Sum** = 40 × 70 = 2800

⇒ If each value is multiplied by **20**, the **New Sum** = (x₁ × 20) + (x₂ × 20) + ... + (x₇₀ × 20)

⇒ **New Sum** = 20 × (x₁ + x₂ + ... + x₇₀) = 20 × 2800 = 56000

⇒ **New Average** = New Sum ÷ 70

⇒ **New Average** = 56000 ÷ 70 = 800

**∴ The correct answer is 800.**

**__Additional Information__**

Addition and Subtraction Rule

If a constant **k** is added to or subtracted from every value in a set, the new average will be (Old Average + **k**) or (Old Average − **k**) respectively.

Division Rule

If every value in a set is divided by a non-zero constant **k**, the new average will be (Old Average ÷ **k**).

Combined Average

The average of two groups with n₁ and n₂ elements and averages A₁ and A₂ is (n₁A₁ + n₂A₂) ÷ (n₁ + n₂).</p
